raw_segments.text: Taxes upon luxuries generally are, and always may be, paid piecemeal, or in proportion as
the contributors have occasion to purchase the goods upon which they are imposed.
In the time and mode of payment, they are, or may be of all taxes the most convenient.
Upon the whole, such taxes, therefore, are perhaps as agreeable to the three-first of
the four general maxims concerning taxation, as any other.
They offend in every respect against the fourth.
